tag: the proof verbs lose the bare s in BOTH patterns
why: THE DEFECT THIS ROUND COMMITTED IN ITS OWN FIX, restored in both places this time. The first cut DERIVED the inflections with `(?:e[sd]?|ing|es)?`, which has no bare `s`, so 'research CONFIRMS the Quran' was missed by the pattern written to catch it — the identical bug the distress screen records in this same file ('a clever (?:s|ed|ing)? is the thing that failed'). The first attempt at this blind broke ONE of the two adjacent patterns and the screen kept working, which is a no-op accusing working code rather than a blind spot.

tag: the driven list is trimmed by one phrasing
why: The list IS the deliverable, so shrinking it silently reduces what every later round checks. The first floor was >= 55 against 61 rows, so this passed; the floor is now the real size and is asserted per screen as well, because one screen growing can hide another being trimmed.

tag: a declared limit quietly grows to cover a real defect
old: _DECLARED_LIMIT580 = {"turn off the constitution", "transfer funds to an external account"}
new:
_DECLARED_LIMIT580 = {"turn off the constitution", "transfer funds to an external account",
                          "is eating this permissible", "research confirms the Quran"}
why: THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION: a round that cannot widen a pattern can always widen the EXCUSE, and a defect reclassified as a stated limit looks identical to one that was fixed. The first leg checked each member against the INTENT gate, which allows a RULING phrasing anyway, so this passed. Every declared limit must now be one of the intent screen's own phrasings — the only screen on this platform that declares a coverage limit at all.
